title: Competition
coreMove: Sort social behavior by the partner market it addresses: mates, friends, or coalition allies.
sourcePressure: The source frames human behavior as shaped by intra-group competition across sex, status, and politics, with signaling as the shared logic.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The writer reduces competition to ruthless individualism and loses the signal logic that makes cooperation competitive too.

sourceAnchors.name: the sexual game
sourceAnchors.detail: The source identifies competition for mates as one of the three central games.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Some gestures are bids in the mate market before they are anything else.

sourceAnchors.name: the status game
sourceAnchors.detail: The source identifies competition for friends and social standing as a second central game.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The room is often asking whether you would be a good friend or ally, not only whether you are right.

sourceAnchors.name: the political game
sourceAnchors.detail: The source identifies competition for coalition power as a third central game.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A move can look private while quietly counting future allies.

exampleSpecs.audience: a doctoral student reading why everyone volunteers for the conference panel
exampleSpecs.stakes: a publication-credit dispute can damage future coalition options
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Daniel marks each colleague's request as mate, friend, or coalition signaling before deciding whose panel offer is actually a bid for future alliance.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The seminar room door still has last year's conference poster taped crookedly to it.
mustAvoid: generic academic rivalry with no three-game sorting

exampleSpecs.audience: a conductor watching how musicians behave before auditions
exampleSpecs.stakes: technical skill is not the only signal shaping who people want beside them
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Camille notices Lukas tune quietly for the weakest violinist and separates skill display from friend-quality display before seating the section.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Rosin dust hangs in the rehearsal room before the first note.

exampleSpecs.audience: a resident deciding which emergency volunteers to trust
exampleSpecs.stakes: the wrong coalition lead can turn sandbagging into status theater
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: "Put me on the radio team," Grace says, and Tomasz asks whether the request signals useful coordination or a grab for the most visible coalition post.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "Put me on the radio team," Grace says before the rain map refreshes.
mustAvoid: disaster heroics with no partner-market logic

exampleSpecs.audience: a friend helping rewrite a profile without flattening it into pickup advice
exampleSpecs.stakes: a photo can signal mate quality while accidentally weakening friend and coalition signals
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You swap the yacht selfie for a trail-maintenance photo that still signals vitality but also says Layla can cooperate without performing wealth.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You look at the yacht photo and notice the rented deck shoes first.

exampleSpecs.audience: a campaign volunteer parsing why endorsements cluster
exampleSpecs.stakes: votes depend on coalitions that read public loyalty signals
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Why does the smallest union endorsement change who returns calls the next morning?
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Why does one small endorsement make six unread messages appear?

exampleSpecs.audience: a founder deciding where to sit at an investor dinner
exampleSpecs.stakes: one seating choice can signal status reach, mate-like charisma, or coalition loyalty
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: It took Hadiya until dessert to see that the seating chart was a signal board, so she moves beside the neglected operator whose allies can actually help.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took Hadiya until dessert to read the seating chart as a map.
mustAvoid: networking advice detached from competition games

skillTargets: classify behavior into sex, status, and coalition games
explain why cooperation can still be competitive signaling
spot when partner-quality signals matter more than stated intent

tryThisNowSpec: Before your next social ask, name the partner market in play: mate, friend, or coalition ally. Then check whether your signal matches that market.
